title: Matrix multiply
summary: Multiply two dense 256×256 matrices of doubles.
description: Each iteration receives two dense 256×256 matrices of doubles (small integers, varied with the iteration) and multiplies them with the cache-friendly i-k-j loop order. All values are integers, so every sum is exact in floating point and the result cannot depend on summation order, fused multiply-add or vectorisation. All 65,536 entries of the product are hashed afterwards.
reveals: Dense floating-point loops, bounds-check elimination, cache use and auto-vectorisation.
caveat: Plain nested loops over the language's native array type, no BLAS or SIMD intrinsics: interpreters pay for every element access, while optimising compilers may vectorise the inner loop. Node uses Float64Array, Python lists of floats. R uses %*% (the BLAS linked into R), its idiomatic fast path.
